title: Hampton Capital - Dedicated Capacity Discovery

Customer wants predictable latency for customer-facing features and strong audit/KMS controls. Next steps: run capacity sizing survey, schedule benchmark POC, share pricing and security docs.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Janelle Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Redwood), Alex Turner (VP Eng - Hampton), Maya Singh (Head of ML), Daniel Cho (Infra), Sofia Reyes (Security)

Automatic summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Discussed dedicated reserved capacity for inference; customer needs isolation and burst for market open events; security and KMS questions; next steps around benchmarks and pricing.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Turner: Hey everyone, thanks for setting this up, we wanted to dig into Redwood Dedicated and how reserved GPUs would work for our inference flows.
00:12 Janelle Park: Thanks Alex, yeah excited to chat. Quick intros — I’m Janelle, AE, with Marco our SE, and Priya on solutions. Can you do quick role intros?
00:22 Alex Turner: Sure — Alex, VP Eng, I own platform and feature delivery, Maya runs the ML models, Daniel is infra, and Sofia handles security/compliance.
00:31 Marco Diaz: Great. High level, we want to understand your QPS, peak concurrency, latency SLOs, and whether you need strict network isolation (VPC / on-prem) or a dedicated tenant in our cloud.
00:45 Maya Singh: For context — we power a customer-facing recommendation API. Typical traffic is steady but with big bursts during market open windows, like 10x baseline for 15–30 minutes. P95 latency target is ~150ms for short prompts, P99 we care about but can accept slightly higher.
01:05 Daniel Cho: Also important — we need network-level isolation. We can't send all inference out to multi-tenant hosted endpoints, so Dedicated or Private is what we'd consider. We also have strict E2E encryption and KMS for key management.
01:15 Janelle Park: Totally understood. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and a private tenant — depending on whether you want Redwood-managed in a dedicated project or fully private in your VPC/on-prem. Which are you leaning toward?
01:30 Alex Turner: Prefer Redwood-managed dedicated capacity hosted in our cloud account for now — we want faster time-to-value but still need isolation controls and customer data never mixed.
01:40 Priya Raman: So we typically do dedicated pools with pinned nodes for latency predictability, plus a burst buffer on top for peak spikes. Burst nodes can be pre-warmed or spun up quickly depending on capacity.
01:52 Maya Singh: How fast can burst scale? Our concern is that during spikes we maintain P95 and avoid queueing.
02:00 Marco Diaz: If you provide us with the QPS profile and prompt length distribution, we size the baseline reserved pool for steady throughput and set an autoscale policy for bursts. For pre-warmed bursting we can hold a small warm pool or configure fast-spinup with GPU rental, but there’s a tradeoff: warm pool increases cost but reduces spin-up latency.
02:20 Daniel Cho: What's the typical spin-up time for a new GPU node in Dedicated? If it's 3-5 minutes that's too slow for our 15-minute bursts.
02:28 Marco Diaz: Right, provisioned spin-up varies by cloud and instance type — typically 2–4 minutes for full instance provisioning. So for 15-minute spikes we recommend a 20–30% warm buffer and autoscale increment steps set to match your burst curve.
02:44 Sofia Reyes: On security — we need KMS integration and audit logs stored for 12 months. Do you support customer-managed KMS and S3 audit exports?
02:55 Janelle Park: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging to customer S3 buckets for the Private/Dedicated plans. We'll share the SOC2/ISO docs.
03:08 Maya Singh: Any differences in model variants between Hosted and Dedicated? We use quantized models in production to save cost, sometimes 4-bit or 8-bit.
03:18 Marco Diaz: Dedicated supports quantized runtimes and optimized kernels. There are a few caveats around accuracy when moving from fp16 to 4-bit quant, we can run evals on your prompts during the POC. Sometimes quantizashun artifacts show up, we’ll measure delta.
03:36 Alex Turner: Also curious about KV cache and long context for our chat logs — we use a lot of prefix caching.
03:42 Priya Raman: We support KV cache and prefix caching; Dedicated keeps per-tenant KV cache in memory on the serving nodes to reduce repeated compute. There are cache invalidation controls.
03:55 Daniel Cho: Network constraints — we need the control plane reachable through our VPC peering, and data plane isolated. Can you explain routing?
04:03 Marco Diaz: For Dedicated we offer a private VPC endpoint + optional customer VPC peering. The control plane can be either Redwood-managed with tight auth or customer-managed. Data plane stays in the dedicated tenant — we can route requests through your private network.
04:18 Sofia Reyes: Audit and compliance: Do you provide per-request trace IDs, token-level cost tracking, and ability to redact sensitive fields before logs land in audit S3?
04:28 Janelle Park: Yes — per-request tracing and token-level cost/latency breakdowns are in Redwood Console. We can also set up pre-log hooks to redact or transform payloads before writing to audit sinks.
04:40 Alex Turner: Cost question — how does reserved capacity pricing compare to burst-on-demand? We want predictability but also don’t want to overprovision for rare spikes.
04:50 Janelle Park: Typically reserved baseline covers most of predictable traffic and is priced as a monthly committed amount (GPU-hour commitments). Burst usage is billed at a higher on-demand rate. We can model a blended cost for your expected profile. We'll include examples in the proposal.
05:05 Maya Singh: For the POC — we'd like to run 24–48 hour real-traffic benchmark using a copy of our top prompts. Can you support that and can you commit to not mixing our data into any shared training telemetry?
05:16 Marco Diaz: Yes, test datasets are isolated and we do not use customer inference data for training. For the POC we can create a dedicated cluster and run benchmark harness, collect latency percentiles, and measure token cost.
05:28 Daniel Cho: Are there network egress considerations for on-prem vs cloud? We have some legacy on-prem nodes too.
05:34 Priya Raman: For on-prem we offer Private deployments with customer-managed networking; egress depends on your topology. For hybrid, we can place serving nodes in your VPC and optionally use Redwood control plane in our region.
05:48 Alex Turner: Who at Redwood is the escalation path for incident/outage and SLA details? We need an SLA with pages and an SLO for latency.
05:57 Janelle Park: For Dedicated enterprise contracts we include an SLA with uptime targets and escalation contacts. We'll include SLO ideas for latency percentiles; for pages we can integrate with your PagerDuty.
06:10 Sofia Reyes: Encryption at rest — do you support customer-managed keys for the model artifacts too?
06:15 Marco Diaz: Yes, model artifacts at rest can be encrypted with your KMS keys. We can also support HSM-backed keys for extra assurance.
06:25 Maya Singh: One more model question — can we pin model versions and roll back quickly if we see regressions?
06:31 Priya Raman: Yes, Dedicated supports model version pinning and canary rollouts. We also provide eval hooks and regression alerts tied to your prompt set.
06:44 Alex Turner: Implementation timelines — if we sign a Dedicated commitment, how long until we have reserved capacity live?
06:50 Janelle Park: From contract signature to baseline capacity typically 4–6 weeks — includes capacity provisioning, private networking setup, and runbook/ops onboarding. If you want a faster pilot we can spin up a temporary cluster earlier.
07:05 Daniel Cho: OK noted. For sizing — here are rough numbers: baseline qps 60 rps, average prompt ~120 tokens, peaks 600 rps for 15–30 mins, concurrency spikes to ~1200 concurrent requests. Does that map to a recommended GPU count?
07:22 Marco Diaz: Those numbers help. We'll run a sizing exercise but ballpark you might need 6–12 A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline depending on model choice (larger for 70B vs 13B), plus 2–4 warm GPUs for burst buffer. We'll send a formal capacity chart.
07:40 Maya Singh: We use a 13B distilled model in prod — that's been quantized. Should be cheaper than 70B.
07:46 Marco Diaz: Good — 13B quantized reduces per-token cost and fits more concurrency per GPU. We'll simulate with your prompt distribution.
07:55 Alex Turner: Any gotchas on model compatibility or custom ops? We have a few custom CUDA kernels.
08:02 Priya Raman: Custom ops can be supported but require validation. For Dedicated we can load custom kernels in the serving environment, but it adds onboarding work and testing.
08:12 Sofia Reyes: For contract language, we'll need clauses on data separation, breach notification windows, and audit rights.
08:18 Janelle Park: Understood — we'll include standard enterprise clauses and our SOC2 evidence.
08:24 Maya Singh: Can you share a sample benchmark run or look at a previous bank POC?
08:29 Marco Diaz: Yes, we have a benchmark deck and sample harness; I'll share it after the call. It includes latency/cost tradeoffs for different model sizes and quantization.
08:38 Alex Turner: Cool. Let's talk timeline — we want a POC in the next two weeks if possible.
08:44 Janelle Park: We'll prioritise that. Marco will send the benchmark template and we'll follow up with available POC windows.
08:50 Daniel Cho: One operational question — who manages OS/patches for dedicated nodes?
08:55 Marco Diaz: In Redwood-managed Dedicated we handle node OS patching and runtime updates; for Private/on-prem you manage host-level patches. We coordinate maintenance windows and can offer conservative update policies.
09:08 Maya Singh: Also want to capture metrics we'll need: token-level cost, latency percentiles, per-route success rates, error rates.
09:15 Priya Raman: All available in Console; we can add custom dashboards and alerting hooks.
09:22 Alex Turner: Ok to recap real quick?
09:25 Janelle Park: Recap: 1) Hampton wants Dedicated (Redwood-managed) with VPC isolation and KMS; 2) Baseline sized for 60 rps, peaks ~600–1200 concurrency — we'll produce a sizing and cost model; 3) POC: 24–48h real-traffic benchmark with isolated cluster; 4) Security docs/SOC2 and contract clauses to be shared; 5) Next steps: Marco sends benchmark template, Janelle sends pricing/proposal, customer provides telemetry and prompt set.
09:52 Alex Turner: That sounds right. Anything else?
09:55 Sofia Reyes: Please include our legal and procurement contacts in the follow-up.
09:59 Janelle Park: Will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
10:06 Meeting end.
